source_neutral.procedure: Work is done on the surviving draft and any available witnesses, accessed through facsimiles or faithful transcriptions. It is provisionally assumed that revision or assembly may have left inconspicuous leftover textual features, such as an obsolete character name or a reference to an episode that is absent from its present position. The packet establishes neither the existence of such leftover features nor the existence of additional witnesses. Proposed revision layers and assembly sequences are held as hypotheses. The overall process is: for each proposed transition, specify a particular textual feature to look for; search and annotate working copies under a stated matching rule, including comparison passages; record matches, ambiguous readings and non-matches; examine the flagged locations against independent documentary and physical evidence; derive relative order where a directional relationship is established; and compare candidate revision and assembly sequences, keeping several where the evidence does not separate them.
source_neutral.action: For a proposed transition, define a specific textual feature to seek, derived from an attested variant or from an explicitly hypothetical earlier arrangement (for example, a name replaced in one passage that may have been retained elsewhere). Manually search and annotate copies using a stated matching rule. For each match, record the match itself, its location, the surrounding text and the scope that was searched. Apply the same matching rule to passages where the feature could be explained by something other than revision. Annotations are placed on copies at the passages whose text satisfies the rule. If no feature can be specified that would discriminate the proposed transition, stop this search for that transition and leave the transition unresolved. Do not apply chemicals to originals or mark them; keep an unannotated copy.
source_neutral.observables: The expected positive signal is a localized annotation showing that a passage satisfies the stated matching rule, so that a previously inconspicuous correspondence becomes visible. Exact matches are recorded separately from ambiguous readings, and searched passages without matches are also recorded. These are proposed observations, not reported findings. A cluster of annotations indicates locations to examine; the size of a cluster does not by itself establish a revision layer.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: A match supports the presence and location of a feature capable of satisfying the matching rule, and nothing further by itself. Positive and ambiguous locations are examined against witness variants, deletion and insertion relationships, paper features, dated correspondence and provenance, where these are available. A relative revision order is inferred solely where those sources establish a directional relationship, such as an insertion replacing a legible deleted reading. Supported relationships are used to compare candidate revision and assembly sequences, with composition order distinguished from narrative order. A sequence that accommodates the supported relationships with fewer unsupported transitions is provisionally preferred, and every conjectural link in it is identified. If the evidence cannot distinguish between sequences, the competing sequences are all retained and no unique history is selected.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: the surviving draft; any available witnesses (facsimiles or faithful transcriptions); individual proposed transitions between textual states; the specified feature and matching rule for each transition; individual passages, classed as exact match, ambiguous reading, or searched without match; comparison passages where the feature could have a non-revision explanation; independent evidence types (witness variants, deletion/insertion relationships, paper features, dated correspondence, provenance); directional relationships between readings; candidate revision sequences and candidate assembly sequences; conjectural links; hypothetical earlier states. Relationships: each transition is tied to a specified feature and rule; each match is tied to a location, surrounding text and searched scope; matches lead to examination of locations against independent evidence; established directional relationships constrain relative order; candidate sequences are compared by how many supported relationships they accommodate and how many unsupported transitions they require; composition order is kept separate from narrative order; attested material is kept separate from hypothetical material.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Specified follow-up: examine positive and ambiguous locations against witness variants, deletion and insertion relationships, paper features, dated correspondence and provenance where available; check consequential matches against the unannotated facsimile; compare candidate revision and assembly sequences using the supported relationships; preserve originals for later analysis; label unresolved readings, unavailable evidence and hypothetical earlier states explicitly. No further follow-up beyond these steps is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions: the existence of leftover features and of additional witnesses is assumed provisionally and is not established by the packet; the observations are proposed, not reported. Repetition, deliberate callbacks, copying errors or shared language can satisfy the matching rule in the same way as a leftover from revision. Absence of matches cannot exclude an earlier state, because revision may have removed the feature, physical damage may obscure it, or the transcription or the matching rule may miss it. An obsolete-looking reference by itself establishes neither its chronological priority nor a particular assembly event, author or date. Missing witnesses can leave several histories compatible with the draft. Annotation or transcription can obscure readings or introduce apparent patterns. No chemicals are applied to originals and originals are not marked; an unannotated copy is retained. Stopping rules: if no discriminating feature can be specified for a proposed transition, stop the search for that transition and leave it unresolved; if a consequential match cannot be verified against the unannotated facsimile, suspend the affected inference; if the evidence cannot distinguish candidate sequences, retain them all and do not select a unique history.
